Present: Mr. S.S. Kamboj, Advocate
 for the petitioner(s).
 Mr. Manish Bansal, Pp, Ut Chandigarh and
 Mr. Alankrit Bhardwaj, Addl. Pp, Ut Chandigarh.

* * **
Sanjay Vashisth, J. (Oral)

1. Petitioner - Kaviraj Singh Pabla, has filed instant petitionu/s 528 of BNSS, 2023, for quashing of the order dated 07.11.2024 (Annexure P-6), passed by Ld. JMIC, Chandigarh, whereby, application moved by the petitioner for releasing his Car bearing registration No. CH01-CB-7918, Chassis No.
MA3NYFF1SLG656151 and Engine No. K15BN4018864 (Page 8 See), was ordered to be released on condition basis, by treating it a case property.
2. On 29.07.2025, after hearing the respective counsel for the parties, following order was passed:-
"i) Present petition has been filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), seeking the quashing of the impugned order dated 07.11.2024 (Annexure P- 6) passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Chandigarh, whereby in an application moved by the petitioner for release of his car was allowed by treating the vehicle as case property and releasing it on superdari.
It is submitted that the vehicle in question is not a case property, and therefore, the said order is not sustainable in the eyes of law.

Further, seeking quashing of the impugned notice dated 12.07.2025 (Annexure 1 of 3 P-8), whereby the said car has been ordered to be put to auction, in connection with FIR No. 43 dated 11.07.2024, registered under Sections 120-B, 406,
and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, at Police Station Sector 49, Chandigarh, District Chandigarh.

1 ii)

entities.text: Kaviraj Singh Pabla vs Ut Chandigarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent/U.T. is directed to file an affidavit detailing the circumstances under which, car bearing registration No. CH01CB 7918, despite admittedly not being a case property, was taken into possession by the concerned Investigating Officer.
The affidavit shall also clearly explain whether the said car is treated as case property or is otherwise connected in any manner with the FIR in question.

iii) List the matter on 06.08.2025.
iv) The car admittedly is not the case property, it shall be immediately released by the concerned Investigating Officer upon petitioner executing the personal bonds to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.
In such an eventuality, the conditions imposed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Chandigarh, in its order dated 07.11.2024(P-6), shall remain inoperative.
v) To be shown in the urgent list."

3. Today, on the very outset, learned counsel relies upon the compromise arrived at between the parties, on the basis of which, FIR No. 43, dated 11.07.2024, under Sections 120-B, 406, 420 of IPC, 1860, registered at P.S. Sector 49, Chandigarh,
along with all consequential proceedings arising therefrom, have already been quashed by this Court vide order dated 26.09.2025, passed in CRM-M-62522-2024 (O&M), titled as, "Kaviraj Singh Pabla and another v. U.T. Chandigarh and othres".

entities.text: Kaviraj Singh Pabla and another v. U.T. Chandigarh and othres
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Copy of the order is supplied by the petitioner's counsel in Court today, which is taken on record.
Registry to tag the same at appropriate place in the case file.

4. Since the FIR in question, in which the vehicle was seized/confiscated, has already been quashed along with all consequential proceedings, the present petition stands disposed of as having been rendered infructuous, and no further directions are required to be passed in the matter.
2 of 3 Needless to say, the impugned order challenged herein carries no legal force in view of the quashing of the FIR and all consequential proceedings arising therefrom.
Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
Pending misc. application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
(SANJAY VASHISTH) JUDGE October 08, 2025 J.Ram
